messages:
Maria H: Heads-up: CyberWeek soft-launch next Mon 08:00 PT. Product team will stagger regions over a 6h window. We need a short, actionable GPU-hours + warm-pool plan — aim to avoid cold-starts for top tiers and keep cost within the revised budget.
Dan K: Can you drop the rough numbers? baseline vs burst vs warm-pool?
Maria H: Rough draft below (will refine after synthetic run):
- baseline steady: 14k GPU-hours/day (multi-region distributed)
- warm-pool (prewarmed instances): 5k GPU-hours/day (to cut tail latency)
- burst reserve (on-demand oversubscribe): 11k GPU-hours/day
- total projected: 30k GPU-hours/day during campaign window
Olivia S: That baseline looks low compared to last year's BF readout — did we factor in new embedding-heavy feature?
Maria H: Good catch. The feature adds ~20% token load for chat routes; numbers above include a conservative +20% on token consumption.
Akash P: Action items: I'll land a prewarm job to seeding KV caches and weights at T-30m for each region. Proposed job:
```
kubectl apply -f prewarm-job-cyberweek.yaml
# job launches 5 warm pods per AZ, runs 10m health + cache seed
```
Leo R: I'll add an automatic fallback route to quantized-8bit variants when node saturation > 85% per node pool. That should reduce peak GPU memory pressure.
Claire M: Watch NAT / ILB limits in eu-west1 and ap-southeast1 — last test showed ILB connection throttling at ~18k concurrent. If we open more warm pods that could blow through the load balancer limit.
Jamie T: Product wants 99th latency under 500ms for paid tiers. If warm pool isn't enough we need graceful throttles or priority routing.
Dan K: Cost tradeoff: Warm pool adds cost but reduces latency SLA violations (and refunds). Rough estimate: warm-pool incremental cost ~= $18k/day. Is that acceptable?
Maria H: Finance signoff is pending but they prefer to cap incremental spend at $25k/day for the week. We're within that.
capacity-bot: Automated projection v1: peak hour demand -> 520 GPU pods across regions, projected hourly GPU-hours = 620. (Confidence: medium).
Akash P: I'll run a synthetic run tonight at 02:00 PT to validate these numbers. Command I'm using:
```
locust -f tests/cyberweek.py --users 6000 --spawn-rate 600 --host https://api.redwood-staging.internal
```
Olivia S: Add a canary traffic slice (5%) pinned to eu-west1 with real traffic replay; helps validate regional I/O and ILB.
Leo R: Also adding auto-prefetching to KV during prewarm; should shave ~80-120ms off cold requests.
Claire M: Ops checklist: update ILB quotas, provision extra NAT IPs for apac, run packet-capture on warm nodes during synthetic run to validate tail retransmits.
Dan K: OK — owners: Akash prewarm job + synthetic run, Leo fallback + quantized models, Claire infra quotas, Maria coordinate finance, Jamie confirm SLO mapping. I'll consolidate into a short runbook and ping SRE on-call before the run.
Maria H: Thanks — will post the runbook here after Akash's synthetic run results. :thumbsup: 
capacity-bot: Automated projection v2 (post-synthetic): peak pods -> 495, expected peak hour GPU-hours -> 590, suggested warm-pool -> 5.5k GPU-hours/day. Confidence: high. :chart_with_upwards_trend:
